parents.title: Rankin-Selberg unfolding turns a modular average into a Mellin singularity expansion

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: For a smooth modular-invariant function with rapid cusp decay, unfolding identifies its Eisenstein inner product with the Mellin transform of the constant Fourier term. The completed Eisenstein series then constrains that transform's singularities, and reverse Mellin mapping turns the nontrivial zeta zeros into the powers tau_2^(1-rho/2) correcting the leading modular average. Thus the displayed asymptotic is geometrically an equidistribution statement: averages on long horocycles tend to the fundamental-domain average, with zeta-zero-indexed error exponents. This bridge gains a one-dimensional description of a global modular average and its convergence rates, but discards the nonconstant Fourier modes and does not remove the analytic-continuation and reverse-mapping proof burden. Smoothness and rapid decay are essential hypotheses, and display-sensitive normalizations remain scan-level risks.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Combines the transform identity, singularity structure, inverse mapping, and the source's geometric conclusion into a mechanism map: spectral singularities control the error rates by which a one-dimensional horocycle average approaches a two-dimensional modular average, while identifying what the constant-term representation forgets.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The interpretation preserves the exact transform chain, names horocycle equidistribution, removes the critic-identified later-example claim, and states the rapid-decay and smoothness boundary without importing adjacent results.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: Equations (2.1)-(2.2) explicitly unfold the Eisenstein inner product to M(tau_2^-1 a_0(tau_2),s); the completed series is stated to be holomorphic except for simple poles at 0 and 1; equations (2.3)-(2.4) apply reverse mapping and give the leading (3/pi) integral plus a sum over nontrivial zeta zeros. The following paragraph explicitly interprets the limit as equidistribution of the cusp-tangent horocycle.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: Accepted source-grounded interpretation. No claim is made that every zero is observable or that coefficients cannot vanish; those claims are absent from this span. Exact completed-zeta normalizations and pole conventions should be checked against the scan before formula-level reuse.

parents.title: A rational Scherk-Schwarz spectrum realizes misaligned supersymmetry explicitly

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The rational Scherk-Schwarz construction realizes misaligned supersymmetry at coefficient level. Its two theta expansions have equal coefficient magnitudes with parity-dependent signs; after convolution this produces constant-term coefficients c_m^2-(-1)^m b_m^2, for which the tachyon coefficient cancels, the massless graded count is recovered, and bosonic and fermionic signs alternate. The representation gains an explicit algebraic route from the orbifold deformation to graded degeneracies and then, through the constant term, to the modular vacuum energy. It checks consistency of this model with the general cancellation picture, but it neither establishes RH nor guarantees that string examples would detect an RH counterexample. The stated zero-frequency expansion assumes RH, and the dense character/theta displays remain normalization-sensitive.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Traces the parity sign through theta-series coefficients, convolution, physical graded degeneracies, and the constant-term observable, separating an algebraic cancellation mechanism from the conditional zeta-zero interpretation and from the much weaker hope of finding a counterexample.
